title: ISic004488. ISic004488
body:
Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa; edition source: autopsy Mignosa
1Ἐνγυμάχο

Text encoding: Valentina Mignosa; edition source: autopsy Mignosa
1ΕΝΓΥΜΑΧΟ

Facsimile Images

Apparatus criticus

  • Text from autopsy

translation

commentary

The inscription can be dated on palaeographical grounds to the late sixth or early fifth century BCE . The trident-shaped chi, dotted alpha and curved gamma point to a Geloan-Akragantine alphabetic context. The text is read as Ἐνγυμάχο (= Ἐγγυμάχο), an otherwise unattested personal name in the genitive, and is therefore best interpreted as an ownership inscription. Its formation from ἐγγύς and μάχη may be compared with the name Ἐγγύδιχος. The function of the object remains uncertain. The square recess and its three shallow holes may have accommodated a square-section handle secured by three projections or nails. Some Roman stone weights provide morphological parallels, but its weight of 187.392 g does not correspond to any known weight standard attested by comparable objects in Archaic or Classical Sicily. Alternatively, it may have been a small hafted tool, perhaps a hammer intended for a specific purpose. The absence of wear might be explained by a votive use, but the generic provenance from the Fusco area does not permit a more precise interpretation because of the lack of archaeological context.

bibliography

  • Manenti and Mignosa 2024 113-115 no.1 figs.1-2
